page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of system memory, translating to 4 GB of RAM per core. The underlying hardware is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, utilizing dedicated CPU allocation. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_ni, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX capabilities. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate a strong single-core CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25% of tested instances. However, multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth fall into the average tier. Specifically, the instance achieves a read-only small block memory bandwidth of 553.27 GB/sec and a large block write bandwidth of 32.75 GB/sec. Geekbench scores align with this average tier, yielding a single-core score of 1658.0 and a multi-core score of 6531.0. Other operations, including static web serving throughput at 10.68 GB/sec and LLM inference speed for a small 135M model, consistently place in the middle 50% performance bracket.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring dedicated AMD EPYC compute power without the premium of high-end memory configurations. The tradeoff lies in its average multi-core scaling and lack of local NVMe storage, which may limit its utility for storage-heavy databases. It is best suited for general-purpose compute tasks, moderate web serving, software compilation, and light text or image processing workloads that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-core execution.
